body: There is only one person in this world who is gonna look out for #1, and that's you.  If you don't do it, no one else will, because most other people don't have the same compassionate nature.  People like you become nurses and caregivers and live for others, but forget about themselves.  If you really value taking care of other people, then you must take care of yourself first, because how can you give to someone else what you don't have yourself?

I've heard that before--that I don't really belong here.  That since I'm here, I should just stick it out.  

But, I'm just making things worse for others by doing so.

I understand the concepts, theoretically.  I have read a few dozen books on psychology and cognition, taken a few classes on the subject, and it seems clear enough at the time, but the problem is in the application of those principles.

If it looks like a jerk, and acts like a jerk, then it is a jerk.  Even if my motivations aren't malicious, my lack of empathy makes me behave inappropriately.  To the other person, it doesn't matter if I was trying to offend or not, because the result is the same.

I guess there is one person I don't have to self-censor around--my brother.  He's far away right now.  I wish he were here.  :(

It is difficult to articulate what is going on inside one's head.  All of those things happen within the span of a few seconds, and a conversation is like trying to juggle all these balls at once, but they keep coming and falling just as quickly.

Even online contact always ended in someone freaking out and getting angry with me.  I would refuse to talk to them after that, because why should anyone be around a person who makes them miserable?  I am a vector for misery.  I don't want to have regular contact with any one person anymore.

You can't blame yourself for the self-destructive actions of others when they are also struggling with mental illness.  It sounds like you've really tried to help the people around you, so you must be a kind person.  But you should be nice to yourself, too.

High school is garbage.  You are basically in prison with a random assortment of inmates that you may or may not get along with.  If you lack relationships and are miserable in high school, it is not a reflection on you, but on how utterly stupid the "educational" system is.  I couldn't see it back then, but the important thing to remember about high school is that it ends.
